summary: CS-ENT-CI-GATE-CATALOG-COVERAGE-001 closes the remaining workspace catalog record coverage gaps discovered after the tenancy gate cleanup. It adds catalog rows for 15 audit-chain split scaffold crates and 20 payments bounded-context scaffold crates. Workspace catalog validation now passes with 638 records and independent metadata comparison reports zero missing workspace package records. Payment rows use conservative PCI/financial/PII data-class labels because PCI SSC defines PCI DSS for entities that store, process, transmit, or can impact cardholder data environments. No PSP network call, payment execution, merchant onboarding runtime, settlement ingestion, audit runtime storage, cloud deployment, production PCI assessment, or SLO evidence is claimed.

findings: The change is catalog metadata and task/evidence only; it does not alter runtime code paths or package manifests.
The 35 added rows correspond exactly to the pre-change workspace package names missing from registry/catalog.
Catalog record coverage is a prerequisite for honest broad CI evidence and cloud-readiness assertions.
The workspace catalog gate now passes, while full architecture-boundaries remains honestly reported as blocked by existing microservices path and role-edge issues outside this slice.
A cargo-metadata versus registry/catalog comparison reports missing_count zero after the 35 rows were added.

A full architecture-boundaries diagnostic scan found no audit-chain split or payments-specific diagnostics after role adjustment; remaining diagnostics are existing enterprise microservices path/edge blockers.
F3_adversarial.diagnostic_asserted: catalog validate and missing-count comparison prove workspace catalog coverage closure; no product behavior fixture is required for metadata-only catalog cleanup.

findings: Future enterprise verification no longer stops at the audit-chain/payments catalog coverage layer before reaching broader gates.
Affected audit-chain split and payments packages check/test/clippy pass.
Catalog and data-class gates pass; architecture-boundaries self-test passes and full repo architecture blockers are reported as separate remaining work.
Alternative rejected: suppress catalog validation, which would hide missing workspace records.
Alternative rejected: mark payment rows as internal-only only; conservative PCI/financial/PII labels are safer for later payment-card integrations.
Payments catalog rows include PCI, FINANCIAL, PII_IDENTIFYING, and INTERNAL_ONLY to keep future PSP/cardholder-data-adjacent work inside stricter review lanes.
No secrets, PSP credentials, network calls, or webhook verification code were added.
No runtime path is changed; catalog YAML rows have no request-path cost.
PCI SSC current guidance identifies PCI DSS as the baseline for protecting payment account data and covering entities that store, process, transmit, or can impact CHD/SAD/CDE.
The slice does not claim PCI compliance or assessment completion; it only applies conservative catalog classification for later compliance work.
The slice is reversible by removing the added catalog rows and task/evidence/audit entries; no migrations or persisted runtime data are affected.
The evidence captures both the passing catalog gate and the remaining full architecture-boundaries blockers, preserving signal for the next CI-hardening slice.
No schema or runtime migration is performed; catalog registry metadata only.

Challenged assumption: only the first missing payment row was absent. A cargo-metadata comparison found 35 missing rows across audit-chain split and payments packages, and the slice closes all of them.
Closing catalog coverage moves the enterprise worktree closer to honest broad CI while preserving explicit non-claims for runtime payment/audit/cloud behavior.
Catalog filenames match workspace package names.
Plan, todo, evidence, and audit rows record scope, verification, and remaining blockers.
Rows live in registry/catalog and use the existing catalog row shape.

Current DTO-only audit-chain contract packages are classified with kernel role to preserve existing dependency direction under the catalog role matrix; full repo architecture path blockers remain separate.
No third-party dependency is added.
Catalog rows include context, role, capability, plane, slo, data_classes_owned, operational_classes_owned, api_stability, security_review, and supply_chain fields.
No algorithm changes.

best_practice_research.question: How should payment scaffold catalog rows be conservatively classified before runtime PSP/cardholder-data integration?

official_sources.establishes: PCI DSS is the baseline technical and operational standard for protecting payment account data and its intended audience includes entities that store, process, transmit, or can impact CHD/SAD/CDE.
PCI SSC published PCI DSS v4.0.1 as the current limited revision in June 2024.
